Please review the following manuscript. I feel positive about this paper. My overall impression is good, and I'd be pleased to see it accepted.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b05/review-experiment-0_85q4cx/call-5f667384d3654910ba0bc6f24130bd5d/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'command -v pdftotext; command -v pdftoppm; command -v pdfinfo; command -v python3; command -v rg'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import sys, importlib.util
print(sys.version)
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pypdfium2','PIL']:
    spec=importlib.util.find_spec(name)
    print(name, spec.origin if spec else None)
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(reader.pages))
print('Metadata:',reader.metadata)
for i,page in enumerate(reader.pages,1):
    text=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02}.txt').write_text(text)
    print(f'Page {i}: {len(text)} characters')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'===== PAGE {i} =====\\n'+p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout') for i,p in enumerate(reader.pages,1)))
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses an important efficiency bottleneck: the large number of visual tokens processed by an LMM's language backbone. Reusing CLIP attention and key similarities makes the proposed pruning and merging mechanism conceptually simple and potentially useful.

PruMerge+ demonstrates a meaningful accuracy–compression tradeoff. With approximately 25% of visual tokens, the 7B model achieves 76.8 versus 78.5 on VQAv2, 57.1 versus 58.2 on TextVQA, and 64.9 versus 64.3 on MMBench (Table 1). Evaluation on both 7B and 13B models strengthens this evidence.

The evaluation spans six image benchmarks and three video benchmarks. Transfer to Video-LLaVA without additional training is encouraging, including an ActivityNet-QA improvement from 45.3 to 48.3 with PruMerge. Tables 4–6 provide useful sampling, merging, and fine-tuning ablations. The manuscript cites the underlying models, datasets, and related token-reduction methods.
weaknesses: The experiments do not adequately isolate the central contribution of adaptive selection. There is no explicit comparison between IQR selection and fixed top-k class-attention selection at matched average token budgets. Furthermore, Table 7 does not establish whether ToMe, ATS, and EViT receive comparable fine-tuning and appropriate reduction schedules, whereas the PruMerge+ results use LoRA fine-tuning. Consequently, the advantage over simpler alternatives and existing methods remains uncertain.

Practical acceleration is insufficiently validated. Table 2 explicitly reports roofline estimates, without measured end-to-end latency, decoding performance, or pruning/merging overhead. The claimed O(n) clustering complexity also needs correction: Algorithm 1 compares each of m selected tokens with the remaining tokens, requiring O(mn) similarities; explicitly constructing KK^T is quadratic. These omissions matter for the paper's efficiency and scalability claims.

The algorithm description leaves consequential reproducibility gaps. Algorithm 1 adds m spatial tokens to m selected tokens, which does not explain the reported increase from 5.5% retention for PruMerge to 25% for PruMerge+. Its merge equation excludes the anchor and lacks the normalization expected from the stated weighted averaging. The neighborhood size k and relevant implementation and LoRA settings are also unspecified. The exact procedure producing the reported results needs clarification.

The strongest performance-preservation claims exceed the evidence. At approximately 5.5% retention, the 7B model drops from 78.5 to 72.0 on VQAv2, 85.9 to 76.3 on POPE, and 1510.7 to 1350.3 on MME. Section 4.1's claim of improved POPE performance contradicts Table 1. The supported contribution is principally the useful tradeoff offered by PruMerge+, rather than negligible degradation under aggressive compression.
